Sadharan Bima Corporation ----- Petitioner
Vs.

full_judgment:
6. Admittedly the present suit was filed under section 6 of the Admiralty Court Act, 1861. Section 6 reads:- 

 Section 6 vests jurisdiction in the Admiralty Court to try a suit wherein the plaintiff seeks relief for damage done to the goods or any part thereof by the negligence’s or misconduct or for breach of duty or contract by the ship owner, master and crew of the ship. In the instant case the declaration sought for in the plaint relates to declaration of general average arising out of jettison of cargo in order to save the ship and her merchandise. Declaration of general average arising out of jettison of cargo can not be said to be damage to goods caused due to negligence or misconduct or breach of duty or breach of contract by ship owner, master or crew within the meaning of section 6 of the Admiralty Act, 1861. The Admiralty Judge, on facts of the instant case, found that no cause of action was shown as regards damage done to the goods and that no relief by way of compensation for damage of any goods was sought and that a declaratory suit is not contemplated under section 6 of the Admiralty Act, 1861. Under section 6 of the Admiralty Act, 1861 a suit for declaration is not maintainable and that a suit for declaration that declaration of general average arising out of jettison is not amenable to the jurisdiction of an Admiralty Court under section 6 of the Act.The Admiralty Judge acting on the strength of section 157 read with section 117 and 141 C.P.C. returned the plaint with the observation that the plaintiff is at liberty to file the suit in an appropriate forum. This Division in the case of M/s Saleh Steel Industries Ltd. Vs. TSS. "Pacific Abetto" and others, 35 DLR(AD)188 also took a similar view that the Admiralty Court is conferred with power to return a plaint under section 151 read with sections 117 and 141 C.P.C.
